title: Aloo Gobi

seo.title: How to Make Aloo Gobi — Easy Pakistani Recipe
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Aloo Gobi. This easy Pakistani recipe includes step-by-step instructions, tips, and serving ideas.
h2Headings: Pro Tips for the Best Results
seo.imageCaption: Delicious homemade Aloo Gobi — a beloved Pakistani classic

description: Aloo Gobi is a beloved Pakistani vegetarian dish featuring potatoes and cauliflower cooked in a fragrant, spiced tomato-based gravy. It is a hearty and flavorful staple, perfect for a wholesome family meal. This traditional recipe brings the authentic taste of Pakistan to your kitchen, offering a delightful blend of textures and aromatic spices.

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables
instructions.text: Wash and prepare your vegetables. Peel and cube the potatoes into roughly 1.5-inch pieces. Wash the cauliflower and cut it into medium-sized florets. Ensure all pieces are similar in size for even cooking.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat oil in a large pot or karahi over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter for a few seconds. Then add the chopped onion and sauté until it turns translucent and lightly golden brown, about 5-7 minutes. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cooking for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Spices and Tomatoes
instructions.text: Stir in the turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook the spices for about 30 seconds, stirring constantly to prevent burning. Immediately add the chopped or pureed tomatoes. Cook the tomato mixture until the oil separates from the masala, mashing the tomatoes occasionally, about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Incorporate Potatoes and Cauliflower
instructions.text: Add the cubed potatoes to the masala and mix well to coat. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Then, add the cauliflower florets and mix gently. Do not add water at this stage, as the vegetables will release some moisture.

instructions.title: Simmer Until Tender
instructions.text: Cover the pot and reduce the heat to low. Let the Aloo Gobi simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the potatoes and cauliflower are tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking and ensure even cooking. If the mixture appears too dry, you may add a splash of water (about 1/4 cup), but typically it cooks in its own steam.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Once the vegetables are cooked through and tender, sprinkle with garam masala and fresh chopped coriander. Give it a final gentle stir. Remove from heat and let it rest for a couple of minutes before serving hot.

tips: Ensure potatoes and cauliflower are cut into similar-sized pieces for even cooking to achieve a consistent texture. Overcooking can make the cauliflower mushy.
For a richer, more authentic flavor, consider adding a pinch of dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) towards the end of cooking. Rub them between your palms before adding.
Aloo Gobi often tastes even better the next day. Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stovetop or in the microwave.
